overview: Recent political developments include Democrats nominating Hakeem Jeffries to be U.S. Speaker of the House, while international and regional updates highlight various diplomatic and security events. In commercial real estate, industry leadership updates feature WestCap's Kevin Marcus taking over as CEO of Green Street. San Francisco news covers Mayor Lurie's actions to combine the planning and building inspection departments under voter-approved Prop. F to speed up permitting. Meanwhile, Hawaii headlines include a federal judge in Hawaii ruling against a seabed mining plan and local reports examining financial pressures facing households.

items.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House
items.summary: Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be U.S. Speaker of the House, setting him up to be the first Black lawmaker to lead the chamber.

items.title: WestCap’s Kevin Marcus Takes Over as CEO of Green Street
items.summary: Kevin Marcus has been appointed CEO of Green Street in its New York City office, succeeding Jeff Stuek as he moves to executive chairman.

items.title: Mayor Lurie uses new power to merge S.F. planning, building inspection departments
items.summary: Mayor Lurie is using new power granted by Prop. F to merge San Francisco's planning and building inspection departments.

items.title: Storm chaos: Atmospheric river causes flooding across San Francisco
items.summary: An atmospheric river caused widespread flooding across San Francisco, stopping flights at SFO and disrupting mass transit and streets.

items.title: In win for hotel workers union, San Francisco extends COVID-era cleaning rules
items.summary: San Francisco extended COVID-era cleaning rules in a win for the hotel workers union, requiring extra room and elevator cleanings.

items.title: Trump plan for Pacific seabed mining violates law, federal judge in Hawaii rules
items.summary: A federal judge in Hawaii ruled that a Trump administration plan for Pacific seabed mining violates the law following a conservation lawsuit.

items.title: More Than Half Of Hawaiʻi Households Living On Financial Brink
items.summary: More than half of Hawaii households are reported to be living on the financial brink, struggling with basic economic pressures.

wiki.title: W. S. Gilbert
wiki.extract: Sir William Schwenck Gilbert was an English dramatist, librettist, poet and illustrator best known for his collaboration with the composer Arthur Sullivan that produced fourteen comic operas. The most famous of these include H.M.S. Pinafore, The Pirates of Penzance and one of the most frequently performed works in the history of musical theatre, The Mikado. The popularity of these works was supported for over a century by year-round performances of them, in Britain and abroad, by the repertory company that Gilbert, Sullivan and their producer Richard D'Oyly Carte founded, the D'Oyly Carte Opera Company. These Savoy operas are still frequently performed in the English-speaking world and beyond.

otd.text: Cyclone Numa, a rare "medicane", made landfall in Greece to become the worst weather event that the country had experienced since 1977.
Two Palestinian men attacked the praying congregants of a synagogue in Jerusalem with axes, knives, and a gun, resulting in eight deaths, including the attackers themselves.
